content:
Hi Raphael

Q1) Why is there such a feature discrepancy between these versions?

Thunderbird for android builds upon the code base of K9-Mail, a long established open source email app, They have different development histories. There's no shared code with Thunderbird Desktop. It's comparing apples to oranges.

Over time there will likely be some feature convergence. The code base has a lot of technical debt and is a barrier currently. Modernization and refactoring of the code is underway to make future enhancements easier to apply. This is being balanced with current feature development to improve the user experience.

Q2) Why is there no warning while exporting that this will be an issue?

This is an aspect of the app being actively looked at. See link below. https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/pull/11248

Q3) Will this feature ever be added?

You can share your ideas and suggestions on Mozilla Connect where community members can vote for them.

The TB team take these into consideration when assessing the roadmap and priorities. Those voted highest have the greatest chance of being selected for development.

content:
Does the issue only occur in Firefox. Can you test using another browsers or app supporting mailto links?

What happens when you click a mailto link?

  • Nothing happens
  • You're redirected to a web page in the browser.
  • The link opens in another app such as gmail.
  • You see a message saying no app can perform this action.

Firefox

Firefox has some quirks around mailto links. When clicked, Firefox requests confirmation before passing to androids link handling. If you cancel the prompt, clicking the link again does nothing until you close the web page or browser. See screen shots.

Android

When clicking a mailto link, Android normally opens a box allowing you to select which app to open the link with. If you've previously set a default app via this box (ticked don't ask again), it will open automatically.

To reset this default app so you can pick Thunderbird ...

  1. Open Android settings > Apps.
  2. Tap the name of the app currently opening mailto links.
  3. Look for "open by default" or a similar setting (varies by phone / Android version).
  4. Tap clear default preferences.

There's no in app setting within Thunderbird Android to enable / disable its link handling.

content:
Hi Greg

Your case with password reversion is not one I've seen reported before but lets see if we can troubleshoot it.

First try and confirm if the correct passwords are being written successfully to the phones database / persistent storage. The successful connection doesn't prove this. It could be using the password held in the phone's memory.

Troubleshooting

The aim is to see if there's any issue or corruption of the apps database or underlying storage.

Testing.

  1. Change an account's password and complete a synchronisation.
  2. Close and reopen the setting screens for the incoming and outgoing server.
  3. Verify the passwords are correct on each.
  4. Terminate the app from androids recent app list.
  5. Open the app and verify the passwords are correct.
  6. Reboot the phone.
  7. Open the app and verify the passwords are correct.

Repeat the above test but instead of a changing password, try a small setting change such as account colour.

Are the changes retained and persist?

Thunderbird Beta

Installing Thunderbird beta is a good idea. It will allow you to test a fresh install without uninstalling the stable version yet. It CAN be installed side by side with the stable version.

  • Configure its settings manually or import via QR code from Thunderbird desktop (if you use it).
  • Don't import settings from the stable app or a file exported from it. (In case the data is corrupt).

Try the two apps in parallel for a period and see if the second app has the same issue.

Testing using K9-Mail is an alternative to using the TB Beta version. It's identical to Thunderbird aside from a red theme colour and logo. Its build by the TB team from the same code base. K9 and TB version numbers are the same. It can also be installed side by side with your current TB installation.
